summary: Every generation believes this market crash is different. History says otherwise. Aashish Somaiyaa, CEO of WhiteOak Capital AMC, walks through every defining crisis he has witnessed in 27 years, Pokhran sanctions, the dot-com crash, the GFC, COVID, the 2022 FII sell-off, and why successful investing is less about predicting the next crisis and more about understanding how markets behave through them.

fork.decision: A crisis is on every front page. Do you act on the prediction, or stay for the recovery?

this.label: React to the crisis
points: Every generation believes this crash is different, and the fear feels completely real in the moment.
The media runs negative around the clock, and exiting feels like the only responsible move.

that.label: Stay invested
points: Six major crises in 27 years, and every single time markets recovered and long-term wealth creation continued.
Every past crisis, in hindsight, became an opportunity.
The edge is not predicting the next crisis; it is understanding how markets behave through one.

fork.pick: Stay. Not because this crisis is not real, but because the last six were real too, and the investors who kept their conviction were the ones compounding on the other side. This is not a conversation about predicting markets; it is about building the conviction to stay invested when everyone else is losing theirs.

takeaways: Six major crises in 27 years, from Pokhran sanctions to the 2022 FII sell-off, and each time investors questioned India's future. Each time markets recovered and wealth creation continued.
Expectations need resetting: 12 to 13% returns today may be the new 16 to 17%.
The direct vs regular mutual fund debate, in Aashish's telling, often comes down to a surprisingly small amount, roughly 240 rupees a year.
On the AI boom, the honest position is discernment: it can be both a bubble in places and a once-in-a-generation shift, and your portfolio should not bet on one headline.
The biggest mistake investors make is underperforming their own funds, by acting on predictions instead of staying through the cycle.
